foundations.heading: An exchange needs more than a venue.
foundations.lead: India already runs specialised exchanges for businesses and financial institutions, not the public. At GIFT City, cross-border trade finance has the rules for such an exchange, but not yet the asset. So Kubar builds the foundations first and the venue last.

items.a: An export receivable: the amount an overseas buyer owes an Indian exporter under a shipped invoice. You buy it outright, inside your programme limit, without recourse for the buyer’s credit.

items.q: Who carries the buyer’s credit, and who carries disputes?
items.a: You carry the buyer’s credit, insured in your name. The exporter carries disputes, returns, set-off and fraud, and answers for its own warranties.

items.q: Is the cover in my name?
items.a: Yes. In a programme the credit-insurance policy is in your name, on buyer limits the insurer approves. Until that policy is signed, a programme can start on exporters’ own policies with claims assigned to you; we say which applies before you buy anything.
You do. The buyer pays your collection account, and you pay the exporter’s account at its own bank. Kubar never holds an account, receives a payment or releases funds.

items.q: How do I know the shipment and the invoice are real?
items.a: Each element of the evidence package comes from a system the exporter doesn’t control: Indian Customs for the shipping bill, the carrier for the bill of lading, the insurer for the limit, the buyer for its acknowledgement and the exporter’s bank for its no-objection. Kubar checks them against each other before anything is offered to you.

items.q: Who is Kubar, and under what mandate does it act?
items.a: Kubar Labs is the brand of Kubar Protocol Private Limited, founded in India in 2024. Under a written mandate from you, Kubar designs the pool and its rules, checks and documents each receivable, services it and reports. The purchase runs on your licence and your credit policies; Kubar never makes the credit decision, holds money or carries credit risk. Kubar’s own ITFS registration is targeted for 2027; until then Kubar acts as the financier’s origination and servicing agent.

items.q: What happens if a buyer doesn’t pay?
items.a: Kubar flags the late payment, checks with the exporter for any dispute and sends the notices your policy requires. As the insured, you lodge the claim under your policy, with the evidence package behind it. The exporter answers only for its own side of the trade: disputes, returns, set-off, fraud and its warranties.

Programme terms on your own paper (the rules, your limit, the caps and the reporting); a mandate appointing Kubar as your origination and servicing agent; the credit-insurance policy, between you and the insurer; and a receivables purchase agreement with each exporter in the programme.
By a fee from you and a fee from the exporter, for running the programme. Kubar earns nothing from holding money or credit risk.
